description.narrative: Funding under this investment will boost growth and prosperity in the Indian Ocean region and contribute to Australian engagement in the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA). The Fund will provide support to activities that focus on IORA’s priorities, including fisheries management, maritime safety and security, trade and investment facilitation, academic and scientific cooperation, disaster risk management, tourism and cultural exchanges and women's economic empowerment.

description.narrative: Australia funded the inaugural regional Maritime Domain Awareness in the Indian Ocean workshop which brought together 50 maritime domain awareness (MDA) practitioners from across the Indian Ocean region, along with experts from Asia, Europe and the United States, to discuss opportunities to enhance information-sharing between national and regional information fusion centres. Representatives from Indian Ocean navies and coast guards, national MDA centres, regional information fusion centres (IFCs) in India, Singapore, Madagascar, Seychelles and the Pacific Fusion Centre, regional organisations such as UNODC, IOC and IORA presented on various MDA topics. The information exchange deepened participant’s understanding of national and regional MDA systems, practices, opportunities and challenges across the Indo-Pacific region and discussed opportunities to strengthen MDA information sharing practices, including between International Liaison Officers embedded at regional IFCs. The workshop expanded participants’ networks and built trust between liaison officers and experts to foster greater information-sharing and strengthen regional MDA.

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: Australia funds the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) Blue Carbon Hub, led by CSIRO. The Hub builds knowledge and capacity in Indian Ocean countries to protect and restore blue carbon ecosystems in ways that enhance livelihoods, reduces risks from natural disasters, and helps mitigate climate change. It also facilitates collaboration and knowledge sharing among key blue carbon stakeholders in the Indian Ocean. In 2024-25, the Hub hosted the fifth IORA Blue Carbon Hub think tank meeting on ‘Nature, biodiversity and carbon markets for sustainable management of coastal ecosystems’ in Thailand. The meeting provided participating IORA Member States with opportunities to learn more about the potential to use market mechanisms to finance protection and restoration and to generate livelihood opportunities for coastal communities. The Hub also hosted six Early Career Ocean Professionals from Bangladesh, Indonesia, Singapore, Kenya, and Sri Lanka in Perth to complete seven-week research projects on blue carbon relevant to their country.

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: Australia funds the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) Blue Carbon Hub, led by CSIRO. The Hub builds knowledge and capacity in protecting and restoring blue carbon ecosystems in a way that enhances livelihoods, reduces risks from natural disasters, and helps mitigate climate change in the Indian Ocean. In 2023-24, the Hub hosted the fourth IORA Blue Carbon Hub think tank meeting on “Nature-based solutions for adaptation to climate risks in the coastal zone” in Bali, Indonesia which was attended by 44 participants from 18 countries and provided recommendations to the IORA Blue Economy Working Group to take forward. The Hub also hosted two Early Career Ocean Professionals (ECOP) from Oman and Madagascar in Perth to complete a 7-week research project on blue carbon relevant to their country. The Hub continues to play a crucial role in facilitating collaboration and knowledge sharing amongst key blue carbon stakeholders in the Indian Ocean.
